_notes: 388 keys had no Filipino (cur = null); all are translated here. Register: the existing corpus is consistently informal second person (ikaw/mo), which is how Filipino consumer apps address users; new strings follow it. Switching the Student app to kayo/po would be a full re-render of ~1,000 strings, not a patch — owner's call.

Hangyul team: every remaining 'tagapayo' / 'counselor mo' / 'tagasuri' in student-facing copy is aligned to 'Team Hangyul' (or 'Team Hangyul Univ' where the English says Hangyul Univ team), matching the English that no longer names a personal counselor. 'Counselor' is kept only in agency/university staff strings where the English keeps it.

Plan (purchasable package): unified on the loan word 'plan' (already the majority form). 'Plano' collides with study plan / cost plan in Filipino, so v17.gate.*, v17.upgrade.currentPlan, v17.pay.afterPay, v29.services.legacyContract and v3.home.noCounselor were moved off 'plano' / 'support plan'.

Official document names stay official: 'standard admission letter' and 'admission letter' replace the literal 'karaniwang liham ng pagtanggap' / 'liham ng pagtanggap' / 'admission certificate'; 'consular legalization' replaces the vague 'legalisasyon' / 'ipa-legalize'. Student visa is 'student visa' everywhere (was also 'visa ng estudyante').
Visa: 'Paghahanda ng visa' / 'paghahanda sa visa' read as 'we prepare your visa'; rendered 'paghahanda ng mga dokumento para sa visa' (visa document preparation) in v15 scope and v17 gate.

Checklist: 'talaan' (list/record) and 'checklist' were two terms for one concept; unified on 'checklist', which is what Filipino students say. Interview: 'panayam' / 'kapanayamin' unified on 'interview'. Essay: 'sanaysay' unified on 'essay'. Task: 'task' unified on 'gawain'. Matches: 'match' unified on 'tugma'.

Language names in the document-language picker were half Filipino, half English (Hapon, Tsino, Ruso vs Korean, Thai). 'Hapon'/'Tsino' name the people rather than the language, so Japanese, Chinese and Russian are now in English like the other entries; 'Ingles' is kept because it is the standard Filipino word.
'mamaya' (later today) was used for 'later' in a multi-month process (passport.noSub, sponsor.goalHint, prior.why); replaced with 'sa bandang huli' / 'sa susunod'.
Sign in / sign out: 'Pumasok' / 'Lumabas?' are ambiguous (enter / leave); unified on 'Mag-sign in' / 'Mag-sign out', which the Student settings copy already uses.
mobile:login.networkError still carried the Android-emulator / LAN-IP developer hint in Filipino; re-rendered from the English (customer meaning only).
Signup consent (CROSS_BORDER_VERIFICATION) in the native app listed 'items transferred, period, retention' that the English does not; aligned to the Student web wording so both flows read the same.
mobile:v16.pay.status.FAILED is 'Nabigo' (standard status word) while the title/fail copy stays soft ('Hindi natuloy ang bayad'); both avoid 'error'.
Owner decision: student:onboarding.education.institutionPh is localized to 'University of the Philippines' and sponsor.goalPh to 'Korean at Pilipino' companies (market-specific examples, kept).
